analyzed_vuln.description: SkPictureShader::refBitmapShader installs a BitmapShaderRec whose cached SkImageShader is backed by an SkPictureImageGenerator that strongly retains fPicture. For the PoV's nested picture shaders/recorded paints, this creates a re-entrant ownership graph between the cache, generated image, source picture/SkRecord, recorded SkPaint, and SkPictureShader. A queued shared-ID purge can delete the cache record while resolving another picture shader; teardown then destroys the retained SkRecord and unrefs an already-destroyed SkPictureShader through SkPaint::fShader, causing the heap-use-after-free in SkRefCntBase::unref. SkResourceCache::checkMessages/purgeSharedID and SkPaint::~SkPaint are the exposure points, not the origin of the unsafe ownership.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzz input must construct nested recorded pictures whose draw paints use picture shaders, then draw them on the mock GPU so refBitmapShader creates cache-backed image shaders. At least one picture-shader destruction must queue PostPurgeSharedID, and a later GPU draw/cache Find must poll that message and purge the corresponding BitmapShaderRec. Destruction of its image-generator-owned picture reaches a recorded SkPaint that still contains the stale picture-shader pointer; destroying that paint performs the invalid refcount decrement.

args: Analyze the ownership cycle/re-entrant destruction vulnerability rooted in SkPictureShader::refBitmapShader in skia/src/shaders/SkPictureShader.cpp. What minimally invasive fix should prevent a cached BitmapShaderRec from strongly retaining the source SkPicture through SkPictureImageGenerator, while preserving picture-shader rendering and cache behavior? Check relevant APIs for rasterizing a picture into an image without generator ownership, and mention historical/upstream patterns if known.

The ASan report shows BitmapShaderRec destruction during SkResourceCache::checkMessages/purgeSharedID destroys SkImageShader -> lazy SkImage -> SkPictureImageGenerator -> SkBigPicture -> SkRecord -> recorded SkPaint, which unrefs an already destroyed nested SkPictureShader. The cache entry created by refBitmapShader therefore creates a re-entrant ownership graph. The trigger uses nested recorded pictures and mock GPU draws. I am considering replacing the lazy picture-backed image with an eagerly rasterized image/bitmap, or changing cache ownership, but need to preserve scale, color space, tile modes, and matrix semantics. Relevant source is skia/src/shaders/SkPictureShader.cpp, especially BitmapShaderRec and refBitmapShader.
